source: Cortes, Luchini, Green & Beaty (2026), The Scientific Creative Thinking Test (SCTT): Reliability, Validity, and Automated Scoring. Creativity Research Journal. doi:10.1080/10400419.2026.2639038. Materials: OSF 439zs. Final bank = 12 items (4 per subtest). Participants give exactly N_RESPONSES (=3) free-text responses per item; self-paced.

subtests.research_question: Research question generation — read the scenario and ask scientific questions about it.
subtests.hypothesis: Hypothesis generation — read the observation and propose hypotheses for why it is the case.
subtests.experiment: Experimental design — read the claim/hypothesis and describe how you would test it.

items.prompt_html: You travel on a spaceship to a new planet outside of our galaxy. What scientific questions could you ask about this planet?

items.prompt: an unexplored part of the ocean floor
items.prompt_html: You created the first vehicle that can reach an unexplored part of the ocean floor. What scientific questions could you ask about this part of the ocean floor?
You travel to a jungle that contains no human life and is completely unknown to the scientific community. What scientific questions could you ask about this jungle?
You discover a remote island with people who communicate without speaking. What scientific questions could you ask about this?

items.prompt: why more students sing in the hallways at a new school
items.prompt_html: You just started going to a new school. You notice that more students sing in the hallways at this school than at your old school. What hypotheses do you have about why that is?

items.prompt: why dogs like one friend and cats like another
items.prompt_html: You notice that dogs seem to like one of your friends, but cats seem to like another friend. What hypotheses do you have about why that is?

items.prompt: why one lake is warmer than another with the same sunlight
items.prompt_html: You notice that the water in one lake is warmer than the water in another lake even though they both get the same amount of sunlight. What hypotheses do you have about why that is?

items.prompt: why stars are disappearing one by one from the sky
items.prompt_html: You look outside one night and see stars disappearing one by one from the sky. What hypotheses do you have about why that is?

items.prompt: testing whether only water and sunlight determine flower growth
items.prompt_html: Your friend thinks only water and sunlight determine how much a flower grows, and nothing else matters. How could you test that hypothesis?

items.prompt: testing whether someone can read minds
items.prompt_html: Your cousin claims they can read minds, but it only works when a person doesn't know their mind is being read. How could you test to see if this super power is real?

items.prompt: testing whether students at your school are friendlier
items.prompt_html: You think students at your school are friendlier than students at most schools. How could you test that hypothesis?

items.prompt: testing whether some animals have a sense of humor
items.prompt_html: You think some animals have a sense of humor that humans don't usually understand. How could you test that hypothesis?
